$comment: Reviewed inputs to the app's third-party notices -- #664. scripts/check-third-party-notices.mjs reads this file; nothing else does.
noLicenceFile: packages in the app's distributed closure whose installed tarball carries NO licence file. The generator fails closed on
such a package unless an entry here, keyed by name@version, says where its notice comes from instead. A version bump therefore fails
closed again until somebody re-reads the new version. 'excerpt' is read from a file INSIDE the installed package; 'upstream' is text
read from the project's own repository at a named commit, because the package carries none at all. 'licenceText' adds the licence's
canonical text, which this repository already pins (LIC005). copiedIntoBuild: files the build copies verbatim out of a package into dist,
named so the notice says which package each came from.

writtenByTheBundler: packages whose OWN code the bundler writes into dist, which no closure lists because they are build tools -- see WRITTEN_BY_THE_BUNDLER in the generator. Keyed by the INSTALLED name@version, so a bump fails closed (NOT008). 'files' are read verbatim from the installed package; 'from'/'through' cut a file down to the part that covers the code that ships.

A copiedIntoBuild entry may carry 'vendored' (#618): the copied file is somebody else's work that its package vendors -- Binomial's Apache-2.0 transcoder inside the MIT three -- so its notice is written here, once per work, because the package's own licence field cannot say it.

vendoredIntoBundle (#618's review): files a package vendors from somebody else that the bundler writes into the app's OWN chunks -- three's examples/jsm/libs/ copies of KTX-Parse and zstddec, which KTX2Loader imports into the renderer chunk. Same 'vendored' shape as copiedIntoBuild; 'file' is the path inside the package and 'in' says which chunk carries it. apps/web/tools/notices/copied-into-build.ts fails the build over a bundled file from a VENDORED_DIRECTORIES directory this list does not name, and over a name the build no longer bundles.

committedFonts (#991, ADR 0043): fonts this repository COMMITS and the app serves, which are files rather than packages and so in no closure. Each names the files the app serves and the licence file committed beside the upstream input, whose text Part 5 reproduces verbatim; apps/web/tools/fonts/fonts.test.ts holds the list to the files the subsetting step writes.

@mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.1.1.why: The tarball holds its bundles, its types and its WebAssembly and no LICENSE. Its manifest says Apache-2.0, and its type declarations open with the project's Apache-2.0 header, which is the notice it does ship.

murmurhash-js@1.0.0.why: The tarball holds no LICENSE file; its README ends with the MIT licence and its copyright line, which is the notice it does ship.

pmtiles@4.5.0.why: The tarball holds its source, its build and its README and no licence text at all. The text below is the repository's own LICENSE at the commit that released js v4.5.0 (its message ends 'js v4.5.0'), byte-identical to the file at the repository's HEAD on the day it was read.

vendored.name: Basis Universal transcoder
vendored.what: basis_transcoder.js and basis_transcoder.wasm, in realistic/basis/: the transcoder of Basis Universal v1.50, by Binomial LLC, as three 0.185.1 vendors it under examples/jsm/libs/basis/ (three.js took v1.50 in mrdoob/three.js#29418, its last change to these files). The realistic world's KTX2 textures are transcoded by it, on the device, to the GPU's own block formats. The WebAssembly has Zstandard's decoder compiled in, under BSD-3-Clause, which is how it reads a UASTC texture's Zstandard supercompression. Upstream v1.50 carries no NOTICE file (one was added in February 2026, after this version), so Apache-2.0 section 4(d) asks for none; the copy of the licence section 4(a) asks for is the appendix. three's own licence field says MIT and cannot say any of this, which is why it is written here.

vendored.what: valhalla-browser.wasm, in routing/: the Valhalla 3.8.3 routing engine compiled to WebAssembly by Emscripten, with the libraries it links, as valhalla-browser 0.2.1 ships it. The app's route planner runs it on the device to follow roads when no instance routes a leg (#2734, ADR 0097). The package's licence field says MIT and cannot say what the WebAssembly carries, so the package's own dist/licenses/ is reproduced below, file by file and verbatim: the SDK, Valhalla, Boost (BSL-1.0), Protobuf (BSD-3-Clause), protozero and vtzero (BSD-2-Clause), zlib, RapidJSON, Howard Hinnant's date, unordered_dense, cpp-statsd-client, cxxopts, musl, Emscripten (MIT or the University of Illinois/NCSA licence, with LLVM's Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception parts), the IANA time-zone data, and the package's NOTICE.md for them. None is copyleft (spike 0035).

vendored.name: KTX-Parse
vendored.what: ktx-parse.module.js, bundled into the game renderer's chunk: KTX-Parse by Don McCurdy, as three 0.185.1 vendors it under examples/jsm/libs/. three.js took it in mrdoob/three.js#31621 (commit c06699ee2549, 2025-08-10, 'Update to ktx-parse v1.1'), its last change to that file, the same day KTX-Parse tagged v1.1.0. The vendored build is minified by three, so it cannot be compared byte for byte; it carries v1.1.0's levelCount handling, which v1.0.1 does not have, while its KTXwriter string still reads 'KTX-Parse v1.0.1' -- a build constant, not the source. The licence is the same MIT text at both tags and in the npm tarball of 1.1.0. It reads a KTX2 container's header, levels and key/value data before the transcoder is given the payload. three's own licence field says MIT for three.js authors and is not this notice, which is why it is written here.
